CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
  Tuesday, September 21, 2021 - 6:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber
  425 South Mission Drive
  San Gabriel, California 91776

  Due to Executive Order N-25-20 members of the City Council may
  Teleconference into the meeting.
  Chin Ho Liao  Mark Lazzaretto
  Mayor  City Manager

  Tony Ding  Keith Lemieux
  Vice Mayor  City Attorney

  John R. Harrington  Julie Nguyen

  Council Member

  Pursuant to State and County Directives, the physical access to the meeting has been suspended.
  To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an opportunity to comment on items
  on this Agenda, the following opportunity has been established:

  Public Comments

  Please email all public comments on items on this agenda only to cityclerk@sgch.org and include
  the following on the subject line of your email: PUBLIC COMMENT: 09/21/2021 Regular Meeting.
  The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the
  three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
  discriminatory language, will not be read.

  Watch the Meeting Online

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 21, 2021
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – AUGUST 2021

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2021-22 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 21-30 dated July 20, 2021) and California Government
  Code §53646, the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the
  City Council, City Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The August
  2021 Cash and Investment Report is presented to receive and file in
  accordance with the City’s adopted 2021-22 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for August 2021.

  D. BUDGET UPDATE – FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 AND FISCAL YEAR 2021-22

  This report provides a budget update for the City’s General Fund and Mission
  Playhouse for fiscal years 2020-21 and 2021-22.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 21-38 – ANNUAL RESOLUTION FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURES DURING CITY EVENTS

  Each year, the City of San Gabriel hosts twelve street events in the Mission
  District and in the San Gabriel Village. In light of the Covid pandemic, only
  four events will take place for the remainder of this year. These festivals take
  place primarily along Mission Drive, Santa Anita Street and Broadway. To
  accommodate the events, as well as setup and cleanup, specific street
  segments must be closed to vehicular traffic. The anticipated events for 2021
  include Dumpling & Beer Fest on Friday, October 15, 2021, Fall Fun Festival
  on Friday, October 29, 2021, Dia de Los Muertos on Thursday, November 4,
  2021, and the Holiday Tree Lighting on Tuesday, December 7, 2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-38,
  authorizing the Public Works Director to approve the specific street closures,
  dates and times for each event. The Public Works Department, Fire
  Department and Police Department have reviewed and approved the request,
  subject to the following conditions:

  3
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 21, 2021
   1. The Director of Public Works/City Engineer is directed to have signs placed
  with advance notification of the parking restrictions within the above-
  described street closure areas and to implement a traffic control plan to
  close said street segments and detour traffic around the closure.
  2. Fire hydrants shall remain unobstructed at all times.
  3. There shall be no consumption of alcohol within the public right-of-way
  outside of designated area approved by the Police Department.
  4. Any extension cords being utilized in an area where foot traffic may be
  expected shall be protected so as not to be a trip hazard. Manufactured
  electrical coverings that meet ADA requirements must be used to cover
  the cords on the ground.
  5. There must be an inspection by the City’s Building Division personnel of
  all relevant installations in the event area to ensure public safety.
  6. The event area shall be accessible.
  7. All driveway areas, parking lot aisles, streets and sidewalks shall be
  maintained free and clear of any visual and physical obstructions and shall
  not impede ingress or egress of pedestrians with the exception of the
  barricaded areas.
  8. A 20 foot wide fire lane shall be maintained within the street.

  F. RESOLUTION NO. 21-44 IN SUPPORT OF THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT
  OF PARKS AND RECREATION OFFICE OF GRANTS AND LOCAL SERVICES,
  OUTDOOR EQUITY GRANTS PROGRAM (OEP)

  The Outdoor Equity Grants Program (OEP) will support the health of
  Californians by creating outdoor program access for undeserved
  communities. The San Gabriel Police Department (SGPD) sponsors a week-
  long summer camp, Camp SG, for middle school-aged youth in San Gabriel’s
  community. The outdoor camp provides opportunities for San Gabriel youth
  to interact with the men and women of the Police Department, leading to
  productive relationships.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-44
  approving the application for California Department of Parks and Recreation
  Office of Grants and Local Services (OGALS), Outdoor Equity Grants Program
  (OEP) funds.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 700-800 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD

  4
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 21, 2021
   PLANNING CASE NOS: ZC18-001 (ZONE CHANGE/PLANNED
  DEVELOPMENT  OVERLAY  ZONE/DEVELOPMENT  AGREEMENT),
  TMAP18-005 (TENTATIVE TRACT MAP), AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
  REPORT (EIR) APPLICANT: PACIFIC SQUARE SAN GABRIEL, LLC

  Attachment A: Proposed Resolution No. 21-42 for Tentative Tract Map
  application and Certification of Environmental Impact Report (EIR)
  Exhibit 1 – Findings of Facts
  Attachment B: Proposed Ordinance No. 678 for Zone Change/Planned
  Development Overlay
  Exhibit 1 – Proposed Zoning Map
  Exhibit 2 – Development Agreement
  Attachment C: Project Plans
  Attachment D: Color Renderings
  Attachment E: Market Analysis
  Attachment F: Draft Environmental Impact Report (DEIR)
  Attachment G: Final Environmental Impact Report (FEIR)
  Attachment H: Planning Commission Resolution No. 21-09
  Attachment I: July 12, 2021 Planning Commission Public Comments

  The proposed project is a mixed-use development consisting of 243
  residential units, 8 live/work units, and approximately 76,000 square feet of
  commercial area on a 5.85-acre site. The project will require a Zone
  Change/Planned Development Overlay Zone/Development Agreement
  application to change the zoning from C-1 to C-1/PD, a Tentative Tract Map
  application for condominium purposes, and an Environmental Impact Report
  for the environmental review.

  Recommended Action:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the Zone Change/Planned Development Overlay and Tentative Tract
  Map applications. Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-42 certifying the Final Environmental Impact
  Report, making findings required by CEQA and adopting Mitigation
  Monitoring and Reporting Program, and approving Planning Case No.
  TMAP18-005, a Tentative Tract Map for project located at 700-800 South San
  Gabriel Boulevard;

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 678 by title only, and waive
  future reading;

  5
City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 21, 2021
   3. Schedule the Second Reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 678 for the
  next regular City Council meeting. The Second Reading will require a majority
  vote of the total membership of the Council.

  Should the City Council determine the proposed project or any part of the
  proposed project be modified or denied, the appropriate motion should be
  made and passed. Staff will be ready to assist in that instance.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 5, 2021,
  at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 21, 2021
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Liao called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:36 P.M .
  on Tuesday, September 21 , 2021 , with all Council Members and staff participating by
  teleconference.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Liao.

  ROLL CALL
  Council Members Present:  John R. Harrington, Denise Menchaca, Jason Pu, Vice
  Mayor Tony Ding, and Mayor Chin Ho Liao.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,
  Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark,

I  Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire
  Chief  Steven  Wallace,  Human  Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Finance Director
  William Kaholokula, Acting Community Development
  Director/Planning Manager Samantha Tewesart, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  City Council special meeting of September 21, 2021:

  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias, Labor Relations Counsel Steve Filarsky.

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officers' Association,
  San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighters' Association, San Gabriel Fire
  Management Group and all Unrepresented Employees.

I  City Attorney Lemieux announced no reportable action was taken.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Liao stated the agenda order was approved.

  Mayor Liao made the presentation.

I  Presentations were made by Fire Chief Wallace and Police Chief Harris.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Fiona Reimers, Los Angeles County Adult-Teen Services Librarian, provided comments

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented, by a vote of 5-0 as

  The City Council approved the August 27, 2021 , and September 2, 2021, Registers

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - AUGUST 2021

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for August

I  D. BUDGET UPDATE - FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 AND FISCAL YEAR 2021-22

  The City Council received and filed the report.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 21-38 - ANNUAL RESOLUTION FOR TEMPORARY STREET
  CLOSURES DURING CITY EVENTS

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 21-38, authorizing the Public Works

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  September 21 , 2021
   F. RESOLUTION NO. 21-44 IN SUPPORT OF THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF
  PARKS AND RECREATION OFFICE OF GRANTS AND LOCAL SERVICES,
  OUTDOOR EQUITY GRANTS PROGRAM (OEP)

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 21-44 approving the application for
  California Department of Parks and Recreation Office of Grants and Local Services
  (OGALS), Outdoor Equity Grants Program (OEP) funds.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

I  A. 700-800 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD
  PLANNING CASE NOS: ZC18-001 (ZONE CHANGE/PLANNED DEVELOPMENT
  OVERLAV ZONE/DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT), TMAP18-005 (TENTATIVE
  TRACT MAP), AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT (EIR) APPLICANT:
  PACIFIC SQUARE SAN GABRIEL, LLC

  Mayor Liao opened the public hearing.

  Senior Planner Matt Chang made the staff presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included other approved projects in the City containing live-
  work units.

  The applicant's presentation was made by Ken Lee, Vice-President, Pacific Plaza
  Premier Development Group; John Bwarie, Chief Executive Officer, Stratiscope; and
  Rick Abe, Project Architect, Media Portfolio.

  The following provided comments in favor of approval of the project: David Ko Lee,

I  neighbor; Jason Liu, resident; Megan Lau, resident; Doug Richter, resident; Silvia
  Gerstner of A Complete Car Care Center; Dan Gerstner of A Complete Car Care
  Center; Michelle Freridge, Executive Director, Asian Youth Center; Darrel Miller,
  neighbor; Debi Hillberg, neighbor; Sandy Rosco, Executive Director, San Gabriel
  Chamber of Commerce; Tracy R. Wilke, neighbor; Teresa Fung, owner, Cheers Bar
  & Grill, Inc.; Alexis Salamanca, President, Board of Directors, San Gabriel Chamber
  of Commerce; and William R. Manis, President and Chief Executive Officer, San
  Gabriel Valley Economic Partnership.

  The following provided comments in opposition to approval of the project:
  Mitchell M. Tsai, Attorneys for Southwest Regional Council of Carpenters; Lozeau
  Drury, LLP, on behalf of Supporters Alliance for Environmental Responsibility; and
  Johnny Sanchez.

  The following provided comments advocating for the use of a skilled and trained
  workforce in construction of the project: William Alvarez; Christian Ortega; Pablo
  Felipe; Luis Terrazas; and Richard Burns.

I  The following provided comments indicating that the environmental impacts of
  the project would affect them: Kimberly Morales, Southwest Carpenters; Brenda
  Garibay, Southwest Carpenters; and Claudia Silva, Southwest Carpenters.

  Mayor Liao closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included traffic flow; parking; allowed uses for the project; appreciation
  for the applicant's and staff's hard work on this project and for the tribute grove;
  impact fees; affordable housing in-lieu fee; electric vehicle (EV) charging stations
  in excess of requirements; including a reference to the Development Agreement
  (DA) as Exhibit 2 in the Ordinance; methodology for the Conditions of Approval;
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  September 21, 2021
   inclusion of a reference to the Conditions of Approval in the DA; encouragement
  for the applicant to consider comments by the Southwest Carpenters; outreach to
  the commun ity and other development projects; tenant mix; live-work units
  methodology; solar-ready details; open-space programming; planned
  development overlay, density, and floor-area ratio (FAR); impact on fire services;
  water-supply adequacy; Code-compliant alternatives; Environmental Impact
  Report (EIR); permitted uses by zone classification; public benefit; drought-tolerant
  landscape; and adding a spot for a sister-city plaque.

I  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Mayor Li ao, to:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-42 certifying the Final Environmental Impact Report,
  making findings required by CEQA and adopting Mitigation Monitoring and
  Reporting Program, and approving Planning Case No. TMAP18-005, a Tentative
  Tract Map for project located at 700-800 South San Gabriel Boulevard.

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 678 by title only, as amended
  in Section 3 to add a reference to the Development Agreement as Exhibit 2 to the
  Ordinance, and waive future reading.

  3. Schedule the Second Reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 678 for the next
  regular City Council meeting. The Second Reading will require a majority vote of
  the total membership of the Council.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4- 7 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, PU, DING, LIAO
  NOES:  HARRINGTON

  NONE
  NONE

  7. NEW BUSINESS - None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto announced the addition of City Council agenda translations
  in Chinese, Vietnamese, and Span ish to the City's website; and passed along thanks
  from San Gabriel Un ified School District Superintendent Jim Symonds to City staff,
  especially the Police Department and School and Community Engagement Team

  mental health and behavioral issues.
  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

I  Council Member Menchaca reported on attending a celebration of life for fo rmer
  Council Member Sabino Cici; and announced the following upcoming events:
  •  San Gabriel Police Department Community Break-Out Session on September 24,
  2021 , from 6:00 - 8:00 P.M.
  •  Herald Christian Health Center at Jefferson Middle School on September 29,
  2021 , from 2:00- 5:00 P.M.
  •  San Gabriel Hope Lions Club Community Fair on October 2, 2021, from 10:00
  AM. - 4:00 P.M. at the Mission Playhouse parking lot.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  September 21, 2021
   •  Community Services Department events:
  ~  Drive-through trunk-or-treat October 29, 2021 .
  ~  Dia de los Muertos on November 4, 2021 .
  ~  Tu rkey Trot, date to be announced.

  Vice Mayor Ding announced that today was the Mid -Autumn Festival and encouraged
  all to view the moon, connect with family, and have moon cake and Chinese tea;
  announced the San Gabriel Hope Lions Club Community Fair on October 2, 2021; and

I  reminded all to continue COVID-19 safety protocols.

  Mayor Liao reported on the 9-11 Remembrance event at San Gabriel Fire Station 51
  and announced he will be attending the League of California Cities Annual Conference.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Liao adjourned the meeting at 10:09 P.M.
